title: Francis de Sales
hookLine: a gentle bishop: nothing is so strong as gentleness
tomorrow: Vincent de Paul and Louise de Marillac

lines: A SOFT ANSWER TURNETH AWAY WRATH.
cards: "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." That's a proverb in the King James Bible, and it sounds easy until someone is shouting. Then the grievous words come quickly.
Today's figure is a bishop who, tradition says, had a hot temper by nature, and spent his life learning the soft answer instead. People came to call him the gentleman saint.
A saying linked to his name goes something like this: nothing is so strong as gentleness, and nothing so gentle as real strength.

teach.b: Francis de Sales was a Catholic priest, then a bishop, when Catholics and Protestants in his corner of Europe were deeply divided.

Tradition says that as a young priest he was sent into a region that had become Protestant, and when people wouldn't come to hear him, he wrote short pages explaining his faith and slipped them under doors.
Whatever you make of his arguments, notice the method: patient, quiet, personal.

teach.h: A DEVOUT LIFE, RIGHT WHERE YOU ARE.
teach.b: He wrote a book called Introduction to the Devout Life, as letters of advice to a woman living an ordinary life in the world. Its big idea: a life of prayer isn't only for monks and nuns.
A soldier, a shopkeeper, a parent, a servant can each be devout in the life they already have.

And the way there, again and again in his writing, is gentleness, with others and with yourself. When you fall short, he advises, don't rage at yourself. Pick yourself up the way you'd lift a friend who tripped.
Harshness, in his view, just adds a second problem to the first. Paul lists gentleness among the fruit of the Spirit: "love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith".
And in Matthew's Gospel, Jesus describes himself this way: "for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls." Gentleness here isn't weakness.

teach.h: STRENGTH THAT CHOOSES NOT TO CRUSH.
teach.b: It's strength that has decided not to crush.

how: Catholics honor Francis de Sales as a saint and a Doctor of the Church, and his Introduction to the Devout Life is still read by Christians of different churches as a guide to prayer in ordinary life.

games.q: you're a young priest sent to a town where nobody will come to hear you preach. what do you do?
o: write short pages and slip them under doors.
games.why: tradition says Francis de Sales wrote short pages explaining his faith and slid them under doors: patient, quiet and personal.

practice: Think of a hard conversation coming up, or one that keeps replaying, and let the other person's sharpest line arrive; notice where it lands, in the jaw, the chest, the hands.
Breathe out slowly, and silently try one soft answer: not a surrender, just a sentence with no edge on it. If you pray, hold the proverb as you breathe: a soft answer turneth away wrath.
If not, stay with the slower breath and the unclenched jaw.

wordCard.voice: Gentleman saint. The nickname for Francis de Sales, the bishop who taught that gentleness, with others and with yourself, is a kind of strength.

carryVoice: Your line: nothing so strong as gentleness. That goes for how you treat yourself, too. Day eight hundred seventy-eight, done.
